title: Fixed Asset Register Auto-Updater
summary: Upload your Fixed Asset Register once as a baseline, then each period upload that period's invoices and GL; the tool files new purchases into the correct existing asset tab, calculates depreciation the same way the register already does, applies disposals to the matching existing row, and lists anything it couldn't confidently resolve for you to handle by hand.
prompt:
Rather than rejecting the file, it should be smart enough to:

Notice when a row is just an account name (like "41501 Computer Equipments") sitting by itself — and treat everything below it as belonging to that account, until the next account name shows up.
Skip non-transaction rows like "Initial Balance" or subtotal rows — those aren't individual purchases, they're running totals.
Figure out which column is the date and which is the amount by looking at the actual data in each row (dates look like dates, amounts are numbers), rather than requiring a labeled header that says "Date" or "Amount" whatever info is missing get it from the invoice
assumptions: The baseline FAR's existing tab/column layout is exactly what future updates should match; no new tab, column, or asset class is ever added
The GL is a flat table with a recognizable header row (not a sectioned ledger export with account names as row headings and no repeated header)
An invoice matches a GL line by amount + date within a tolerance window, boosted by vendor/reference where present; more than one plausible match is treated as an exception rather than guessed

The period each run covers is derived automatically from the register's own last recorded closing position through to the latest transaction date found in that run's own files — never asked of the user
Only text-based PDFs and plain image files (PNG/JPG/TIFF/BMP) are read automatically via the built-in local OCR engine; scanned PDFs without a text layer are not
gaps: Reading a 'sectioned ledger' style register (account-code-and-name row followed by unlabeled purchase rows, no repeated header, running-total rows like 'Initial Balance'/'Subtotal' interspersed) was requested but is not implemented in this version — the finance user tried an earlier attempt at this and asked to undo it, so the tool still requires the GL to be a flat table with a recognizable header row; a sectioned-ledger register upload will be reported as unrecognized rather than parsed
Vendor/tax/approval information is not extracted from invoices, and disposals are recognized only from GL narration keywords (disposal, written off, scrap, sold), not from an explicit disposal flag
expects: The current Fixed Asset Register as an Excel workbook (.xlsx/.xlsm), uploaded once as the baseline

Each period: the new invoices as PDF or image files (including scans/photos), plus the GL covering those same transactions as .xlsx/.xlsm/.xls/.csv (a flat table with a Date, Amount and Account/Classification header row) — or the same FAR/GL workbook if the GL lives inside it as a sheet

history.prompt:
Develop an automated Fixed Asset Register (FAR) Update Feature for our centralized Accounting & Finance Dashboard.

The purpose of this feature is to continuously update an existing Fixed Asset Register from its current closing position onwards, without requiring the user to rebuild or manually update the FAR.

The user will upload the existing FAR ONCE as the BASELINE. The uploaded FAR is the source of truth for the existing FAR structure and accounting treatment. The feature must inspect the uploaded FAR and automatically understand its existing tabs, asset classes, columns, formatting, depreciation rates, depreciation calculations, schedules, formulas and overall structure. Do not create a new FAR structure or ask the user to define these items separately. Simply preserve and follow the structure already present in the uploaded FAR.

After the baseline FAR has been uploaded, whenever the user wants to update it for a subsequent period/year, the user will provide:

1. The fixed asset addition invoices for that period/year.
2. The relevant General Ledger (GL) for those transactions.

The feature must use the two inputs for different purposes:

- INVOICES should be used to obtain the detailed information required to update the FAR, including asset description, invoice date, vendor, invoice/reference number, amount and any other relevant information available on the invoice.
- GL should be used primarily for classification and accounting validation, particularly to determine which existing asset-class tab/head the transaction belongs to and to validate the relevant accounting entry.

The feature should therefore match and use the invoice and GL together rather than relying on either source alone.

For example, if an invoice contains the purchase of a laptop and the corresponding GL identifies the transaction under Computer Equipment, the feature should automatically add the asset to the existing Computer Equipment section/tab of the FAR and populate the relevant information using the invoice.

The feature must NOT overwrite or recreate the historical FAR. It should take the existing FAR closing position as the starting point and add/process only the transactions occurring after that position.

Every time an update is performed, the feature should automatically:

- Identify the new fixed asset additions from the provided invoices and GL.
- Match the invoices with the relevant GL transactions.
- Determine the appropriate existing asset class using the GL classification.
- Extract the detailed asset information from the invoices.
- Add the new assets to the appropriate existing FAR tab/listing.
- Follow the exact presentation, columns, formulas and structure already used in the uploaded FAR.
- Continue the existing depreciation schedule for the newly added assets.
- Update the relevant depreciation and carrying amounts within the FAR in the same manner as the existing assets.
- Preserve all previously recorded assets and historical information.
- Avoid duplicating assets or transactions that are already present in the FAR.

DEPRECIATION RULE:

For newly added assets, the month of purchase must be treated as a full month for depreciation purposes.

If an asset is purchased at any date during a month, depreciation for the entire month must be charged.

If an asset is disposed of during a month, no depreciation should be charged for the month of disposal. Depreciation should therefore stop in the month immediately preceding the disposal month.

The depreciation rate, useful life, calculation method and presentation must NOT be separately provided by the user. The feature must identify and follow the rules already present in the uploaded FAR.

The same principle applies to all other FAR-related structure and accounting treatment: the uploaded FAR is the reference point and should be followed.

If disposal transactions are identifiable from the provided GL/supporting information, update the relevant existing asset rather than treating the disposal as a new addition, and apply the existing FAR's disposal treatment together with the depreciation rule above.

The feature must also perform reasonable validation while processing the update. It should identify duplicate transactions, invoices that cannot be matched with the GL, GL transactions that cannot be matched with an invoice, amount mismatches, or transactions that cannot be reliably classified.

Do not repeatedly ask the user routine accounting or formatting questions. The feature should make these decisions by inspecting the existing FAR and applying the workflow defined above.

Only flag an item for user review when the information genuinely cannot be determined from the uploaded FAR, invoices and GL. Such items should be clearly identified as exceptions rather than being guessed or incorrectly incorporated into the FAR.

The key workflow is:

BASELINE FAR → uploaded once and treated as the master/source of truth.

SUBSEQUENT PERIOD → upload invoices + relevant GL → feature automatically identifies, classifies and adds the new assets → calculates/updates depreciation → preserves the existing FAR → produces the updated FAR.

For every future update, the latest updated FAR should become the new starting point, so the user only needs to provide the new period's invoices and GL.

The final result must be the SAME FAR updated from its existing closing position onwards, with the new additions and related depreciation incorporated into the appropriate existing sections/tabs, without requiring the user to manually restructure, classify or rebuild the FAR.
